I figure I'd post this in case other people were thinking about signing up for the 'free' hotspot. You can see it on their Product page by scrolling down: http://www.freedompop.com/#products (Freedom Spot Overdrive Pro).

They advertise it as: "100% FREE 4G mobile broadband Internet access"

Their web site says: "FreedomPop's partnered with leading wholesale 4G Wimax and 4G LTE mobile broadband networks"

Here's How the Scam Works:

  1. You buy one of the Wi-Fi hotspots. It costs like $63 (including $10 shipping).

  2. They mail you a refurbished Wi-Fi hotspot device branded with "Sprint" and "Sierra Wireless".

  3. You activate it via their web site and get automatically enrolled in the Free 500MB plan.

  4. What they don't tell you is that this device only operates on the 4G Sprint WiMax network. 4G LTE Data is NOT included

  5. On the FREE plan you don't have access to the 3G network. To get a functional device you have to upgrade to the Premium plan which gives you 500 MB of 3G/4G access for $3.99 / month.

NOTE: the Sprint WiMax network was shut down so this device will not function in 4G mode

I am wondering why they are still offering it for sale. I bought mine in May of 2015 and was kind of pissed when I found out about this. It felt like bait-and-switch. The web site made it seem like you buy the hardware once and then you get 500 MB of data for free. Out of the box, the Freedom Spot Overdrive Pro is useless. To "fix" this problem, FreedomPop is offering to sell you another device at a discount. The new devices probably don't function in 4G mode for free either.

I signed up for the Premium plan for a few months just to try it out. The hotspot works fine in 3G mode. They also offer a Data Rollover plan for an extra $3.99 / mo. which allows you to save unused data (up to 20 GB). So, for about $8 a month you can get a functional 3G WiFi hotspot. But, $8 is not FREE. This type of misleading advertising should be illegal.

To make matters worse: my device was non-working when I received it. I discovered that FreedomPop didn't refurbish it. They took the used device from Sierra Wireless and sent it directly to me. I followed all the instructions and could not connect. I did some research and found you had to connect it to a computer, log in via a browser, and update the PRL (Preferred Roaming List) under the advanced settings. It's a good thing I'm savvy. A new user would never have figured this out.

More about the WiMax shutdown here:

https://forums.freedompop.com/discussion/12620/wimax-shutdown-important-info-11-9

TL;DR:

  • Freedom Spot Overdrive Pro is a scam. You don't get FREE data.
  • It costs $3.99 / mo. to make it functional
  • Sprint 4G WiMax network was shut down. Device only functions in 3G.
  • They are still selling these non-working devices on their site

How to still use it:

I downgraded to the "FREE" plan. I unplugged my device and yanked the battery. It's sitting in a box and costing me nothing per month. You can add or remove services on the FreedomPop web site whenever you want. If you decide that you need emergency Internet (example: your cable goes out) you just log in via your phone and activate the $3.99 / mo. 3G/4G Premium plan. Then, before the next billing cycle, cancel the service. This way you have an on-demand 3G hotspot without paying monthly fees.
